newsitem.title: USA: Texas spot power prices flat amid natgas rebound.
newsitem.headline: Texas spot power prices flat amid natgas rebound.

text.p: Spot wholesale electricity prices Tuesday in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) stayed flat versus Monday's levels amid a rebound in the natural gas market following recent losses.
Today's upturn in gas prices failed to offset outlook of lackluster power demand linked to very mild temperatures in the state through the end of the week, market sources said.
"There's not much load out there," said a Houston marketer.

Extended forecast showed temperatures in Texas would stay well-above normal into the first week of 1997 with day readings in 60-70 degrees Fahrenheit and night readings in the 30s-50s, about 10 to 15 degrees above seasonal norms.

On the New York Mercantile Exchange, February Henry Hub gas futures closed up 8.8 cents at $2.765 per million British thermal unit (mmBtu) in an abbreviated session. However, swing gas prices in south Texas continued their downward course, down 20 cents to the $2.40 level from Monday.
NYMEX will close Wednesday due to the New Year holiday.
ERCOT firm, peak power for a 16-hour block for Thursday was heard mostly discussed in a $22.00-$23.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) range, compared with Monday's $23.50-$24.00.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Thursday's heavy load hours was assessed at $21.00-$22.00, off from $22.50-$23.00 Monday.
Firm off-peak ERCOT deliveries for Thursday were still valued at $9.00-$11.00.
ERCOT electricity for non-firm delivery during Thursday's light load hours held in a notional range of $8.50-$10.50.
